messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in three cities with specific facilities. We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each city with appropriate facilities. The function signature: location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

We need to pass an array of facilities? The type says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That seems ambiguous: maybe facilities can be a single string or an array of strings? The example says "Cafe"[] meaning array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe" type? But likely they want an array of strings. We'll pass array of strings.

So for New York: reading room and fiction. So facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

For Los Angeles: Wi-Fi and children section. So facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"].

For Chicago: cafe and reading room. So facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to call the function three times. Probably we should call it once with location "New York, NY" and facilities array. Then again for LA, then Chicago.

We need to output the results. We'll call the function for each.
